key_insight: Vacuum diffusion welding combined powder molding, sintering, and bonding to produce an antifriction composite coating on 12X18H10T stainless steel.
engineering_relevance: The process offers a route to wear-resistant coated components for demanding mechanisms, including space-technology applications.
method: Combine chromium-steel powder, CaF2, and MoS2 with a stainless-steel substrate.
Consolidate and bond at 1203 K and 27 MPa for 1600–1800 s under approximately 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ Pa vacuum.
Evaluate adhesion, coating strength, tribological behavior, and interface microstructure.
evidence_signal: Wear tests spanned 900–3600 s at 1 MPa and 0.23 m/s; the abstract reports a post-running-in wear metric of 3.3 × 10⁻⁸ at 1200 s in B-70 gasoline, without specifying units.
watch_item: The abstract inconsistently identifies the powder as X10H13 or X20H13, so composition must be verified before replication.
paper_title: Obtaining anti-friction coatings using the method vacuum diffusion welding
